done_when: Find the root cause of each (Forge not waiting for its processes to exit, or the test checking too early or on a reused id) and fix it at the cause; both tests pass on every OS in CI three runs in a row; no test is skipped or loosened to pass

findings.body: A terminated process retains its PID and start time until reaped, so this comparison treats zombies as running ([wait documentation](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/wait.2.html)). Consequently, `_stop` exhausts both polling periods at src/forge/codex.py:373–376. In the driver-timeout path, reaping cannot occur until `_stop_leftover` returns (lines 241–245). An unreaped lock owner also blocks recovery because `_take` treats it as active (lines 408–410). The new test encounters this condition: it waits for its child only at tests/test_codex_record.py:325, after doctor returns, but its substring assertion permits the erroneous additional warning. Check termination state while preserving identity across exec, and assert that recovery recognizes the stopped process.
findings.title: Exclude terminated, unreaped processes from the liveness check

why: Main's CI is red on and off: tests/test_codex_record.py::test_6_nothing_left_running fails on macOS and Linux (_down(pid) is False right after the stop), and tests/test_codex_reader.py::test_10_the_cold_read_runs_on_the_other_family fails on Linux (forge doctor doesn't report stopping a crashed forge read's processes), so every pull request hits them
